==English==

===Etymology===
* Adverb: From {{inh|en|enm|later}}, {{m|enm|latere}}, from {{inh|en|ang|lator}}, equivalent to {{suffix|en|late|er}}.
* Adjective: From {{inh|en|enm|later}}, {{m|enm|latere}}, from {{inh|en|ang|lætra}}, equivalent to {{suffix|en|late|er}}.

Cognate with {{cog|stq|leeter||later}}, {{cog|fy|letter||later}}, {{cog|nl|later||later}}, {{cog|nds-de|later||later}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈleɪ.tə/|a=RP}}
* {{enPR|lāʹtər|a=US}}, {{IPA|en|/ˈleɪ.tɚ/|[ˈleɪ̯.ɾɚ]}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-later.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|eɪtə(ɹ)|s=2}}

===Adverb===
{{head|en|adverb}}

# {{en-comparative of|late}}
#: {{ux|en|You came in late yesterday and today you came in even '''later'''.}}
# Afterward in time (used with ''than'' when comparing with another time).
#: {{ux|en|My roommate arrived first. I arrived '''later'''.}}<!-- (but we could both have been on time)-->
#: {{ux|en|I arrived '''later''' than my roommate.}}<!-- (ditto) -->
# At some unspecified time in the future.
#: {{ux|en|I wanted to do it now, but I’ll have to do it '''later'''.}}
# {{lb|en|Manglish|Singlish}} {{cap|what if}} (something problematic or unanticipated happens); [[if not]] (something undesirable will happen).
#: <small>Compare {{ncog|ms|nanti|t=later; if not}}</small>
#: {{syn|en|sekali|q1=Singlish}}
#: {{ux|en|'''Later''' you fall asleep how?|'''What if''' you fall asleep?|inline=1}}

====Synonyms====
* {{sense|afterward in time}} {{l|en|afterwards}}, {{l|en|hereafter}}; see also [[Thesaurus:subsequently]]
* {{sense|at some unspecified time in the future}} {{l|en|later on}}, {{l|en|someday}}; see also [[Thesaurus:one day]]

====Antonyms====
* {{l|en|earlier}}
* {{antsense|At some unspecified time in the future}} {{l|en|once}}

===Adjective===
{{head|en|comparative adjective}}

# {{en-comparative of|late}}
#: {{ux|en|Jim was '''later''' than John.}}
# Coming afterward in time (used with ''than'' when comparing with another time).
#: {{ux|en|The Victorian era is a '''later''' period of English history than the Elizabethan era.}}
#* {{RQ:Withycombe Christian Names|edition=1st|chapter=Introduction|page=xiii|passage=The eldest son was usually given the name of his paternal grandfather, '''later''' children those of other relatives.}}
# Coming afterward in distance (following an antecedent distance as embedded within an adverbial phrase)
#: {{ux|en|I felt some leg pain during the first mile of my run and I strained my calf two miles '''later'''.}}
# At some time in the future.
#: {{ux|en|The meeting was adjourned to a '''later''' date.}}
